key_concept: In the Bohr model, the Coulomb attraction supplies the centripetal force, $\frac{mv^2}{r}=\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\frac{e^2}{r^2}$, which gives $r=\frac{ke^2}{mv^2}$.
steps: Equate the electrostatic force to the centripetal force for hydrogen ($Z=1$): $\frac{mv^2}{r}=\frac{ke^2}{r^2}$. This gives $r=\frac{ke^2}{mv^2}$.
why_not_others: Option (3), $x=2$, results from forgetting to square $v$ properly or from mishandling a factor of 2. Options (1) and (2) come from errors in the powers of ten or from using $r\propto n^2$ with a guessed $n$.
common_trap: Students substitute $v=25.6\times10^{5}$ instead of $\sqrt{25.6}\times10^{5}$, or square the factor $25.6$ again, which wrecks the powers of ten.
time_saving_tip: Notice that $9\times2.56=2.304$ appears in both the numerator ($ke^2$) and the denominator ($mv^2$). The mantissas cancel, so only the powers of ten remain: $10^{-28}/10^{-19}=10^{-9}$.
